title: We're Back to Normal Rates, Says Ed Yardeni
summary:
Yields in the US and other advanced economies have climbed to multidecade highs, tightening financial conditions, amid higher inflation triggered by the US-Iran war and concern about budget shortfalls. 
Traders have responded by paring rate-hike expectations, with the amount priced into swaps across eight major economies falling by almost 200 basis points since mid-September, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. 
Ed Yardeni, President at Yardeni Research, discusses his S&P call and why he believes rates are 'back to normal' and not 'higher for longer.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: CFTC Staff Told to Retract Analysis of Suspicious Oil Trades
summary: CFTC analysts flagged unusually well-timed trading ahead of a March 23 Truth Social post in which President Donald Trump postponed planned U.S. strikes on Iranian energy facilities. Billions of dollars in contracts changed hands in the 15 minutes before the announcement. According to sources, analysts identified traders and referred their findings to the CFTC’s enforcement division, but a senior official intervened and asked them to retract the referral. Charles Gorrivan reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Domino's Drops on Sales Growth Miss; Bumble Goes Private | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Domino's Pizza (DPZ) shares are lower after the restaurant chain reported total domestic stores comp sales growth for the third quarter that missed the average analyst estimate.
- Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) shares are moving as the company reports earnings. J&J raised its profit guidance as demand for newer drugs in cancer and autoimmune diseases overshadowed more anemic growth in the company’s medical device business.
- Bumble (BMBL) shares are halted on news Ithaca is taking Bumble private for $1.3 billion, with a deal price of $6.05 per share. Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd said she would “remain actively involved with Bumble” after the deal, which marks a significant change for the company that was valued at $14 billion when it went public. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: New Mountain Bets on Defensive Growth
